Topics. campaign setup and tracking / Architecting a structured, multi-stage e-commerce Google Ads account by deploying foundational layers first. Establishing baseline data through Non-Branded Shopping (for new customer acquisition) and Branded Search/Shopping (to capture cheap, high-intent conversions). Layering in remarketing via video/display or Feed-Only Performance Max once baseline conversion data stabilizes. Scaling with top-of-funnel Demand Gen (YouTube/Discover) campaigns only after exhausting bottom- and mid-funnel intent. return on ad spend (ROAS) / Optimizing budget efficiency and attribution by strictly isolating branded from non-branded traffic via negative keyword lists and priority settings. Utilizing low-budget, high-ROAS branded campaigns to feed the algorithm cheap conversion data, thereby improving the machine learning models that drive more expensive, new-customer non-branded campaigns. Transitioning bidding strategies from "Maximize Clicks" (for initial data gathering) to "Maximize Conversion Value" or "Target ROAS" once a threshold of 15–30 conversions per month is reached.

Look for. The recommended chronological order for launching e-commerce Google Ads campaigns: starting with Search and Shopping (bottom/mid funnel), adding remarketing/PMax (mid funnel), and scaling with Demand Gen (top funnel) last. The core structural rule for non-branded campaigns: explicitly adding branded terms as exact-match negative keywords to prevent attribution distortion. The specific definition of a "feed-only" Performance Max campaign: a PMax campaign stripped of all text, image, and video assets, forcing the algorithm to rely solely on the Google Merchant Center shopping feed for product remarketing.
Skip. General agency promotional pitches, requests to book strategy calls, or basic Shopify interface navigation instructions.
